newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Islamic nations blast Israel, call for unity.
newsitem.headline: Islamic nations blast Israel, call for unity.

text.p: Islamic foreign ministers opened their annual meeting on Monday with a blast at Israel over its treatment of Palestinians and calls for cooperation to further the welfare of the world's 1.5 billion Moslems.
Afghanistan represented a contentious issue for the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC), with both sides in the conflict vying for Kabul's seat at the five-day Jakarta meeting.

Indonesian President Suharto, leader of the world's most populous Islamic state, said in an opening address that the Palestinian people "continue to suffer Israel's acts of provocation as it reneges on its commitments under the 1993 Declaration of Principles and subsequent agreements".
"Agreements between Palestine and Israel are irrevocable international accords which cannot be changed and must be respected," he said.
Suharto added that for a just and comprehensive peace in the Middle East, "Israel must unconditionally withdraw from the Syrian Golan Heights and Southern Lebanon".
Indonesia's Foreign Minister Ali Alatas, who is chairing the 53-member OIC gathering, referred to "a dangerous impasse" in the Middle East.
Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara accused the Israeli government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of omitting "the peace plan from its plan of action".
The situation in Afghanistan is also causing concern to OIC states.

Conference sources said officials from both warring sides were "jockeying" for Kabul's seat, which has been purposely left vacant. The sources said the issue was likely to come up during a plenary session.
The purist Islamic Taleban militia seized Kabul on September 27. Forces loyal to ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani and ethnic Uzbek leader Rashid Dostum are trying to retake the city.
"It is essential that the parties involved in the conflict initiate broad-based inter-Afghan talks aimed at establishing a government of national unity," Alatas said.
Other areas of concern include Bosnia-Herzegovina, Jammu and Kashmir, divided Cyprus and Somalia.

Conference sources said India had objected to the presence of a separatist delegation from Kashmir fighting Indian rule. The Indians wanted the Kashmiris to be barred from taking part in debates, the sources said.
Suharto in his address also called for a constructive North-South dialogue for global economic development.
Speakers also called for unity to put forward what Alatas called the true face of Islam.
He said there were dangerous misconceptions equating violence and terrorism with the Moslem world.

This would never be resolved, however, "until we are able to effectively communicate Islam for what it is -- a force for peace, justice and common good, a way of life that has intellectually enriched Western civilisation itself".
